Reuters reported that Russia's antitrust regulator has officially launched an investigation into Apple, accusing the company of failing to pre-install the state-backed instant messaging app MAX and the Russian app store RuStore on its devices. Details are as follows.

Russia launches antitrust investigation into Apple

Since Russia passed a law in 2019 requiring device manufacturers to provide local apps on products sold in the country, Apple and the Russian authorities have been engaged in a protracted tug-of-war.

When the law came into effect in 2021, Apple reached an arrangement under which Russian users setting up a new iPhone would see a list of recommended Russian-developed apps, rather than having them installed automatically.

In March 2022, following Russia's invasion of Ukraine, Apple stopped selling and exporting products in the country, and removed the RT News and Sputnik News apps from the App Store outside Russia. That September, Apple also removed several apps operated by Russian tech company VK, citing UK sanctions.

Last year, Russia began requiring that all new smartphones and tablets sold in the country come pre-installed with the state-backed instant messaging app MAX, while extending the mandate to pre-install the RuStore app marketplace to Apple devices. Apple has not complied with either requirement.

Tensions escalated further in June, when Apple removed MAX from the Russian App Store, and later the same month removed several apps developed by VK. Apple said the removals were to comply with sanctions.

This prompted Russia's Federal Antimonopoly Service to order the company to resolve what it called "discriminatory treatment" of domestic software by 15 July. Apple reportedly made partial concessions, allowing a Russian search engine to be pre-installed in iOS 26.6, but did not implement the requirements relating to MAX and RuStore.

Now, according to Reuters, Russia has formally opened an antitrust investigation into Apple over its failure to fully comply with the warning.

The report is as follows:

It remains unclear what penalties Apple could face if Russia finds it has violated its competition laws. In 2024, Russia calculated that Google owed a fine of around 20 decillion dollars (a 2 followed by 33 zeroes), accumulated over years of refusing to restore blocked Russian state and pro-Kremlin channels on YouTube.

Apple has not yet responded to the investigation.
